feedback:
Approved to race. This candidate changes one geometry variable from the best raced design (iteration 7, score 687.1): the lateral spacing of the sensor row narrows from x = ±0.03 m to ±0.02 m. Sensor y (0.08), sensor_size (0.012), sensor_weights, kp 3.8, kd 0.8, ki 0, base_speed 1.3 and line_loss 'last_direction' are unchanged, so the result isolates lateral spacing. The design is valid: all x and y values are inside the contract limits, and 12 mm footprints at 10 mm spacing overlap with no gaps.

The evidence supporting the test is iteration 6, where widening the array to ±0.045 m cut slalom line_loss_events from 1.4 to 1.0 but dropped slalom progress from 0.46 to 0.31, and raised s-bend steering_oscillation. That pattern suggests the slalom progress limit moves in the opposite direction when the array narrows. The cost is the other side of that trade: a narrower array should lose the tape at a smaller lateral offset, so slalom line_loss_events may rise. Because the score averages the three development tracks, a slalom progress gain is worth about a third of its size, while an oval or s-bend loss is worth about 600 points on that track. So the oval and s-bend finishes matter more than the slalom gain.

Gain and speed are not the levers to pull now: kp 4.0 cut slalom progress (iteration 5), kd 0.8 cut it while helping the s-bend (iteration 4), and base_speed 1.2 cost more than it gained (iteration 2).

After the race, compare per track against iteration 7: oval finish count and max_error, s-bend finish count and steering_oscillation, and slalom progress, max_error and line_loss_events. Decide the next step from those numbers. Iteration 7 remains the fallback if this design loses ground.
requested_changes: After the race: if the oval stays at 20/20 or 19/20, the s-bend stays at 19/20 or better with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.33, and slalom progress rises above 0.46, keep lateral spacing at ±0.02 m and test ±0.015 m only if the score is still above 687.

After the race: if the oval drops to 18/20 or below, the s-bend drops below 19/20, or the score falls below 687, revert to the iteration 7 design exactly (x ±0.03 m, y 0.08, 12 mm, kp 3.8, kd 0.8). Do not adjust gains to rescue it, because gain changes have not moved the slalom since iteration 4.

After the race: if slalom progress rises but slalom line_loss_events climb well above 1.5 with the oval intact, keep the narrow array and test sensor_size 0.016 at ±0.02 m to widen each footprint's coverage without changing spacing. Keep ki at 0 and base_speed at 1.3.
